_provenance.kinds: The scanner (python_call_kind in generate_necb_8_4_coverage.py) classifies each article= citation call site into exactly two kinds: 'cited' (any call other than audit.warn/audit.warning) and 'warn' (an audit.warn/audit.warning call). It does not separately distinguish 'decision' from 'info' — both fall under 'cited'. This baseline keys by the scanner's own two kinds, not the three-way decision/warning/info vocabulary used to describe the intent.
_provenance.note: Re-baselined 2026-09-19 for Sol's review of D-93 (PR #53). Three new warn sites per edition, 225 -> 231, each a decline his findings required: (1) where the corresponding proposed pump states no usable efficiency; (2) where a pump in the group states a power no pump can draw, so the combined shaft power is not computable - that case previously reached sum() with a None and terminated compliance processing with a TypeError; and the article= keyword that was missing from the existing (2) 'no usable combined shaft power' warning, which made that site invisible to the scanner. Nothing was lost: no 'cited' count moved and no frozen baseline moved. Re-baselined 2026-09-19 for D-93 (DF-11 increment B), which decides the reference pump's VALUE SOURCE per correspondence and by the sentence that governs it. Six new warn sites per edition, all of them DECLINES the previous mechanism could not make because it inferred a whole-building intensity instead: no corresponding proposed loop; an ambiguous correspondence; N:1 consolidation (left to its own adjudication); an undeterminable distribution flow (never fall back to the sum of the pumps' flows); a proposed pump stating a power no pump can draw; and more than one pump on the reference loop, where the Article describes one. Total 213 -> 225. Nothing was lost: no 'cited' count moved, and the foreign-citation baseline is unchanged. Prior re-baselines, kept for the chain: 211 -> 213 on 2026-09-17 for the D-92 review fixes (the exclusion notice); 209 -> 211 on 2026-09-16 for D-92 itself (the first (3) fallback site); and before that, generated AFTER renaming compliance.py's local lighting_prefix -> prefix, which made the article= keyword at compliance.py:346 and its warn-branch sibling scanner-visible. Re-baselined 2026-09-28 for D-97 (PR #63), 231 -> 233. One warn site per edition: the 8.4.x.14.(1)-(3) decline was split in two so the N:1 branch alone carries 'D-93 D-97' and its 'not a conservative bound' wording, while every other decline shape keeps D-93's. Both halves carry article= and ruling=, so the split ADDS a warn site rather than moving one. Nothing was lost: no 'cited' count moved, and the verify lane re-ran with no frozen baseline movement (Fable, PR #63).
_provenance.rebaseline_reason: Re-baselined for the D-100 envelope review's edition-owned citation fix. Two hard-coded NECB 2020 literals were replaced by ruleset.article() lookups, so their literal counts drop to zero by design: 'Table 3.2.2.2.; 3.1.1.7.(4)' in envelope/prescriptive.py and the Note 'A-8.4.4.4.(1)' inside reference.py's thermal-mass citation. Article 3.1.1.7 keeps its number across editions but was restructured from eight sentences to four, so the enclosure credit moved 2020 (4) -> 2025 (3) and inclination moved 2020 (6) -> 2025 (4); the literal cited the wrong sentence on every 2025 run and never cited inclination at all. The thermal-mass Note moved A-8.4.4.4.(1) -> A-8.4.5.4.(1). Citations are not lost: they are now resolved per edition and BOTH clauses are emitted, which the static literal scanner cannot see.
